question: What is the primary function of a day care centre?

options.A: Treating acute medical and surgical emergencies
options.B: Serving as a primary and secondary school
options.C: Offering permanent residential care for orphans
options.D: Providing daytime supervision and developmental activities

explanation: Day care centres provide temporary daytime supervision and structured activities while families are busy elsewhere. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do day care centres differ from residential care facilities?

options.A: Day care centres do not require any supervision
options.B: Residential facilities only open during daytime hours
options.C: Day care centres are strictly medical hospitals
options.D: Clients return to their homes every evening

explanation: Unlike residential homes where individuals live permanently, day care attendees go back home at the end of each day. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which health benefit is directly promoted by day care nutrition programs?
explanation: Structured meal plans in day care settings help supply essential nutrients to growing children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why are day care centres considered useful for community disease surveillance?

options.A: They isolate infected adults from the general public
options.B: They replace community health clinics during strikes
options.C: They allow quick detection of spreading infections among children
options.D: They manufacture vaccines for rural immunization campaigns

explanation: Gathering many children in one space makes early symptoms of contagious illnesses visible to caregivers and nurses quickly. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h2)

question: An employer-sponsored day care centre is typically located where?

options.A: At a remote rural farm settlement

explanation: These facilities are set up by organizations to make it easier for their employees to access child care. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a defining feature of home-based day care operations?

options.A: They receive massive grants from international health bodies
options.B: They operate exclusively as night-time boarding schools
options.C: They employ over fifty specialized pediatric nurses
options.D: They care for a small group inside a private residence

explanation: Home-based setups use domestic living spaces to look after a limited number of children at a time. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which government agency typically inspects day care physical structures before approval?

options.B: The federal ministry of petroleum resources
options.C: The national union of road transport workers

explanation: Town planning and health departments review building safety and environmental sanitation before licensing. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why must a day care centre be located away from industrial hazards?

options.A: To make it easier for parents to drive past quickly
options.B: To reduce the cost of renting commercial property
options.C: To protect children from toxic emissions and heavy traffic
options.D: To comply with agricultural land use policies

explanation: Physical safety requires keeping vulnerable children away from pollution, noise, and fast-moving vehicles. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for regularly disinfecting toys in a day care?

options.A: To prevent children from swallowing small parts
options.B: To improve the bright colors of the toys
options.C: To make the plastic materials last forever
options.D: To prevent the spread of infectious diseases

explanation: Children frequently share and mouth toys, making regular cleaning vital to stop germ transmission. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a required safety measure in a day care centre?

options.A: Leaving chemical disinfectants unlocked on the floor
options.B: Installing secure covers over electrical wall sockets
options.C: Keeping functional fire extinguishers within reach
options.D: Fencing the outdoor play area securely

explanation: Chemicals must always be stored securely away from children to prevent accidental poisoning, making unlocked storage incorrect. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: A key nutritional goal for meals served in a day care centre is what?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of local carbohydrates
options.B: Meeting adequate caloric and micronutrient guidelines
options.C: Providing high amounts of processed sugary snacks
options.D: Relying solely on vitamin supplements for energy

explanation: Balanced meals support healthy physical growth and prevent nutritional deficiencies during early childhood. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of monitoring developmental milestones in a day care setting?

options.A: Early identification of delays for prompt referral
options.B: Ranking children by their academic intelligence
options.C: Certifying children for secondary school admission
options.D: Predicting exact adult height and body weight

explanation: Noticing developmental lag early enables healthcare providers to intervene before problems become severe. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a community health nurse visiting a day care?

options.A: Teaching advanced calculus to older children
options.B: Reviewing immunization records and conducting health checks
options.C: Cooking the daily lunch meals for the staff
options.D: Managing the financial accounts and payroll of the facility

explanation: Nurses oversee vaccination statuses and health standards to protect the entire group of children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: How does the community health nurse assist day care staff during a disease outbreak?

options.A: By prescribing antibiotics to all parents and teachers
options.B: By coordinating containment measures and public health reporting
options.C: By shutting down the facility permanently without notice
options.D: By ignoring the symptoms until routine inspection day

explanation: Nurses guide infection control practices and report outbreaks to relevant health authorities to stop further spread. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is a major operational challenge faced by many day care facilities?

options.B: Excessive space for outdoor playground activities
options.C: Too many trained pediatric doctors on site

explanation: Financial constraints and frequent changes in caregivers often disrupt consistency and quality in day care centres. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why are low staff-to-child ratios important for quality assurance in day care?

options.A: To ensure every child receives adequate supervision and attention
options.B: To make sure teachers have more time for personal rest
options.C: To reduce the total number of hours the centre stays open
options.D: To comply with architectural restrictions on room size

explanation: Fewer children per caregiver allows for better safety monitoring and more responsive interaction. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h8)
